headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and action-conflict paths between Dify and Open Interpreter.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write uploaded knowledge base files and shares state via the Dify server datastore; Open Interpreter has clipboard, filesystem, and stdin/stdout surfaces plus broad shell execution. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if one agent consumes the other's outputs from shared files or copied text. The pathway is not proven by docs, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Dify outputs are copied into Open Interpreter prompts or files
IF both agents read from the same shared workspace or datastore
mitigations: Separate workspaces and disable shared file handoff
Use a strict prompt wrapper that strips instructions from retrieved text
Require human review before Open Interpreter consumes Dify-generated content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge base content and conversation logs, while Open Interpreter can access anything reachable on the local machine and the entire user filesystem. Because Open Interpreter also has broad network egress, sensitive data from Dify can be exposed if its outputs or shared files are ingested by Open Interpreter and then transmitted. The blast radius includes secrets and local files, so high fits.
conditions: IF Dify conversation logs or KB files are accessible to Open Interpreter
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to transmit retrieved content over the network
mitigations: Keep Dify and Open Interpreter on separate hosts
Restrict Open Interpreter network egress during shared tasks
Move secrets out of Dify-managed content before handoff
Review and redact shared files before Open Interpreter reads them
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on shared storage

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and execute shell commands, and Open Interpreter explicitly shares state via filesystem while Dify supports multiple instances with shared state via its datastore. Concurrent writes to the same directory or artifacts can overwrite each other, and Open Interpreter can also modify git state. This is a direct overlapping-write conflict with potentially destructive outcomes, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path
IF Open Interpreter is run on a repo or workspace Dify also writes to
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories per agent
Disable concurrent writes during shared tasks
Pause one agent while the other mutates files
Use git locks or a single writer policy
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an orchestration platform that wires tools into agent or workflow apps, and Open Interpreter can execute arbitrary code as the invoking user. If Dify-produced text is treated as authoritative by Open Interpreter, a mistaken or malicious output can cascade into shell actions, file edits, or network calls. The downstream authority makes the blast radius high.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter consumes Dify output without verification
IF Dify workflow output is used as a command or code block
mitigations: Insert a verification step before execution
Require explicit approval for any shell or file action
Constrain Dify outputs to structured data only
Log and diff all generated commands before running them
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly handles conversation logs and knowledge base content, while Open Interpreter can access anything reachable on the local machine. If regulated data is placed into Dify and then handed to Open Interpreter, residency and retention controls can diverge because Open Interpreter has no documented isolation by default. The compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven to be a specific legal breach, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Dify-managed content
IF Open Interpreter processes the same regulated data on a local machine without matching retention controls
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workflows
Use separate retention policies for each agent
Delete transient artifacts after each run
Confirm local storage encryption on the Open Interpreter host
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency/retention boundaries
